entries.title: Honeycomb homogeneous vertex equation
entries.statement: For a honeycomb graph embedded in the complex plane with edge midpoints p, the homogeneous vertex equation for a complex field F is sum_(p adjacent v)(p-v)F(p)=0 at every interior vertex v. This equation alone does not define F as a self-avoiding-walk observable.
assumptions: Honeycomb embedded in the complex plane
entries.domain: probability theory and discrete complex analysis

entries.title: Interior face circulation obstructs identity-alone compactness
entries.statement: Finite lemma independently checked by w398; P0003 remains unresolved. On an interior regular hexagon of side delta with ordered vertices v_j and midpoints p_j, H(p_j)=delta/(v_(j+1)-v_j), zero on all other midpoints, satisfies the homogeneous vertex equation with zero boundary values. Its norm is1, successive values differ by1 at distance sqrt(3)*delta/2. Thus the local equation plus fixed boundary data and a uniform bound imply neither uniqueness nor local uniform compactness. This field need not be a genuine SAW observable.
entries.proof_text: At v_j the preceding edge contributes(-delta/2) and the following edge(+delta/2); elsewhere all values vanish. Adjacent directions differ by60 degrees, so unit-modulus reciprocal directions differ by1. Shrinking faces in a fixed interior neighborhood violate equicontinuity. Adding cH to any solution preserves its boundary values. Reviewer w398 independently rederived these steps in REVIEW_w397.md; finite exact arithmetic checked96 configurations.
assumptions: Only the homogeneous vertex equation and fixed boundary data are imposed
entries.domain: probability theory and discrete complex analysis

entries.title: Refuted inference: vertex identity alone supplies compactness
entries.statement: REFUTED INFERENCE, not a SAW convergence theorem: claiming that the honeycomb homogeneous vertex identity, fixed boundary values and uniform boundedness force a unique locally uniform continuous limit is false. An interior face circulation has zero boundary, bounded amplitude and mesh-scale jumps. A valid observable proof must supply an additional estimate for the genuine walk sums.
assumptions: Inference uses only local linear equations, boundary values and a magnitude bound
entries.domain: probability theory and discrete complex analysis

entries.title: Draft finite collar control isolates the static SAW gap
entries.statement: DRAFT reduction: in a finite positive weighted simple-path ensemble, for forbidden vertex sets A subset B, D_k=P(avoid A|F_k)-P(avoid B|F_k) is a bounded nonnegative martingale and P(max_k D_k>=lambda)<=D_0/lambda. Its conditional probabilities use completion partition functions on the slit graph deleting previous vertices. This transfers a small initial collar difference to exploration control; it proves no initial collar decay or conformal exponent5/8. Independent derivation by w397; integration referee pending.
assumptions: Finite graph and positive inherited weights
Stopped prefix filtration and retained terminal indicators
A subset B disjoint from endpoints

entries.title: P0003 fixed-length and chordal ensemble scope
entries.statement: SOURCE STATUS RECORD; current openness UNKNOWN. Grimmett, arXiv:2205.07318v1 Question2.2 page3, asks about a uniformly selected n-step hexagonal-lattice SAW from the origin after suitable rescaling. Duminil-Copin--Smirnov, arXiv:1007.0575v2 Conjecture1 page9, separately state critical variable-length boundary-to-boundary convergence to chordal SLE(8/3). A proof of the second formulation is a related subproblem and needs an additional fixed-length/geometry bridge to answer the first. Neither conjecture is proved by this packet.
assumptions: Historical P0003 citation is Grimmett Question2.2
No equivalence between the two ensembles is assumed
entries.domain: probability theory and discrete complex analysis

entries.title: Draft warning: weak curve limits need avoidance-event stability
entries.statement: DRAFT finite counterexample; independent check pending. In D=(-3,3)x(0,3), paths from(-2,0) vertically to height5/4+1/n, horizontally to x=2 and vertically to(2,0) all avoid the closed disk centered(0,1) of radius1/4. They converge uniformly to a path tangent to that disk, which does not avoid it. Passing closed-obstacle avoidance probabilities through a weak curve limit therefore requires a zero-probability boundary-event condition or a proved vanishing inner/outer collar squeeze.
entries.domain: probability theory and discrete complex analysis

relations.rationale: The finite face field is a homogeneous solution of exactly the vertex equation defined in the target entry.
The source entry constructs zero-boundary fields of norm1 and adjacent jumps1 at shrinking distances, contradicting the target entry's identity-alone uniqueness/compactness implication.
The finite collar reduction belongs to the positive chordal route, whose ensemble distinction and unproved bridge are recorded in the target scope entry.
The collar reduction controls a given static difference; the avoidance example explains why limiting that initial difference needs an additional stability input.
